0700: One voucher can be redeemed ten times, if you send the requests at the same moment. And the fix is not more checks. It is where the check lives. Your code reads the voucher, sees it is unused, applies the discount, then marks it used. Fire ten requests at once, and all ten read unused before any write lands. That is a race condition. The fix: make the check and the update one atomic step. A conditional update, a unique constraint, or a lock. Then test it with parallel requests.
0900: If you take card payments, PCI DSS applies to you. The trick is shrinking how much of your system it touches. Scope is every system that stores, processes or transmits card data, plus anything connected to them. Let card numbers reach your servers, and your whole platform is in scope. Use your payment provider's hosted fields or tokens, and card numbers never reach you. Your scope shrinks, your audit gets smaller, and a breach has far less to steal. Design for scope first. Compliance gets cheaper after.
1300: The refund flow is where money leaves your company, and it gets a fraction of the testing checkout gets. Three things to check today. One. Can a refund be bigger than the original payment? Two. Can the same order be refunded twice, by retrying or by racing two requests? Three. Can a customer refund an order that is not theirs? Each one is a direct path to losing money. Give refunds the same checks as payments: ownership, limits, and one refund per order line.
1500: Security engineers who only say no stop getting invited to the meeting. Here is how to say no to a launch without being the blocker. First, name the specific risk, in business terms. Second, offer the smallest change that makes it acceptable. Third, give a date: not yet, but by Thursday. Fourth, if they accept the risk anyway, write it down with an owner. You keep the relationship, the team ships, and the risk becomes a decision, not an accident.
1700: Some of the easiest money to take is hiding in the decimals. If your app rounds each transaction on its own, an attacker can send thousands of tiny transfers where every rounding goes their way. Currency conversion makes it worse, when a round trip through two currencies comes back slightly bigger. The fixes are boring. Store money as whole numbers in the smallest unit. Round once, in one place, with a written rule. And reconcile totals, so a slow leak shows up before it adds up.
1900: Which payment flow in your product gets the least testing? Checkout gets all the attention. Refunds, reversals, payouts and promo codes often get none. Pick the one you test least, and test it this week. Which one is it for you?
